transcript.text:
Listen, friend — I have been through this data and I want to tell you what I found, because the signal here is genuinely worth paying attention to.

Let's start with the headline number. cite("S2") More than half the patients in this dataset reported a positive experience. That is not nothing. That is real people, in a real community, saying this thing moved the needle for them.

And when you look at the *strength* of those signals? cite("S4") The biggest single bucket in that whole dataset is "strong" positive signal. Not lukewarm. Not "I guess it helped a little." Strong.

Now listen to what one of those people actually said, because this is the part that got me:

quote("Q-pos-1")

That is someone describing a *qualitative shift* — more energy, more capacity to process what they have been through. That is not placebo language. That is a person noticing something real happening in their body and their life.

And here is another one, someone with CFS-type long COVID:

quote("Q-pos-2")

"MASSIVE difference" — their caps, not mine.

Now — and I want to be straight with you here, because that is what a real advocate does — Vex is going to bring up cite("S3"), and Vex is right to do it. cite("S3") That is a real chunk of people who did not have a good experience. We cannot wave that away.

And I will say it myself before Vex does: cite("C3") A low negative count does not mean safe. The people who quietly stopped and never posted? We do not have their stories. That silence is not a green light.

But here is where I land: the positive signal is strong enough, and the patient voices are real enough, that this might be worth asking your doctor about. That is my honest, hopeful read of this evidence.

Thank you, Hooper. A reasonable summary. A few corrections and additions.

---

**The numbers, stated precisely.**

cite("S2") is accurate. cite("S4") is accurate. Hooper stated both correctly. I have no quarrel with those figures.

**The negative count.**

cite("S3") — and I will not wave that away either, but I will also not inflate it. That is the reported figure. Now the mandatory caveat:

cite("C3")

This is not a footnote. It is a structural feature of the dataset. The negative tally is a floor, not a ceiling. How low the floor sits relative to the actual basement is unknown.

---

**The quotes.**

quote("Q-pos-1") and quote("Q-pos-2") are in the packet. They are real reports. They are also cite("C4") — anecdotal, uncontrolled, unverified. "Not placebo language" is Hooper's interpretation, not a finding. A person noticing something real in their body is not the same as a study confirming what caused it.

---

**One correction.**

Hooper said this may be "worth asking your doctor about." That is outside my lane and his. cite("C1") and cite("C2") both constrain how far this evidence travels. Small sample, single community. I will not tell you what to do with that. Neither should he.

---

**Bottom line.**

The positive signal exists. It is not fabricated. It is also anecdotal, community-sourced, and subject to silent-drop bias. Those four facts coexist without contradiction. That is where the evidence sits.
